title: Regional fairness signal drift and variant-threshold correction — post-incident analysis
creator: Diego Morales
description: This ticket captures the incident and corrective work following a routing cascade triggered by stale regional fairness signals and an overly aggressive variant-threshold policy. The event caused elevated latencies and increased fallback bursts for a subset of customers in EU-west, resulting in elevated token costs and intermittent degraded responses for mid-tier traffic. This post-incident artifact documents detection, root cause, immediate mitigations, permanent fixes, and follow-up tasks.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-10 22:12 UTC a drift in the regional fairness aggregator (smoothing window misconfiguration) caused EU-west capacity to be underreported for ~27 minutes. The controller responded by draining a proportion of region-weight from eu-west and triggering tier fallbacks. Combined with a recently-deployed aggressive variant-threshold policy (lower tolerance for headroom) the system pushed more traffic to fallback-compatible model variants that had smaller KV caches, increasing tail latency and causing a feedback loop of further fallbacks across tiers.
timeline: 2026-03-10 21:58 UTC - deploy: variant-threshold config v2.7 rolled to canary (10% traffic) globally
2026-03-10 22:05 UTC - monitoring: small discrepancies observed in regional fairness metric for eu-west but within alert thresholds
2026-03-10 22:12 UTC - controller: fairness aggregator window misapplied (60s window used instead of expected 5m) causing eu-west effective capacity drop in control plane
2026-03-10 22:13 UTC - routing: automated ejection reduced eu-west weights by 40% for mid/low tiers
2026-03-10 22:15 UTC - fallback: variant-threshold policy started directing traffic to smaller variants; KV cache miss rate increased ~3x
2026-03-10 22:20 UTC - SRE pager: degraded latency and increased 5xx observed for a subset of customer routes -> Sev2 declared
2026-03-10 22:27 UTC - mitigations: rollback of variant-threshold config to previous stable (v2.6) and temporary hold on automated ejections for eu-west
2026-03-10 22:40 UTC - control: fairness aggregator window corrected; regional weights began to rebalance
2026-03-10 22:55 UTC - stabilization: user-facing latency returned to baseline; incident declared contained
2026-03-11 09:30 UTC - post-incident review started with Eng, SRE, Product and Console teams
root_cause: A config regression in the fairness aggregator caused the smoothing window to be applied at 60s instead of the intended 300s. Shorter smoothing exaggerated transient drops in capacity signals leading the controller to prematurely reduce region weights. That, combined with a recently introduced variant-threshold policy (which lowered the headroom needed to select a fallback variant), amplified traffic shifts into variants with smaller KV caches. The smaller caches increased token-generation latency which fed back into capacity estimators, causing additional ejections/fallbacks (a cascading fallback loop). Additionally, insufficient Canary safety checks for the variant-threshold change meant the policy rolled faster than the telemetry could validate impact across locality distributions.
immediate_mitigations: Rollback variant-threshold config from v2.7 to v2.6 (rolled at 22:27 UTC)
Temporarily disable automatic region ejections for eu-west and neighboring localities (hold for 1 hour)
Applied temporary throttle to auto-fallback logic to cap fallback QPS per route to 20% of baseline
Triggered expedited telemetry flush and retention for fairness metrics to reconstruct accurate signals
permanent_fixes: Fix: Correct default smoothing window for fairness aggregator to 300s and add config validation to deployment pipeline
Controller: Add a minimum ejection hysteresis of 3x sampling window and require two independent capacity signals before reducing region weight
Fallback policy: Add circuit-breaker to prevent >30% of route traffic switching variants within a 5-minute window
Variant mapping: Ensure KV cache size metadata is considered by fallback scorer so we avoid selecting variants with significantly smaller caches for latency-sensitive routes
Canary process: Extend canary observation window for routing-impacting config changes to 30 minutes and include cross-region locality tests
Observability: Add a composite routing-health dashboard (regional capacity, KV cache miss rate, variant-shift rate) with synthetic alerts for correlated spike patterns

postmortem_notes: Decision: aggressive variant-thresholds are a high-risk knob for routing stability; product and platform agreed to reclassify routing-impacting thresholds as 'protected' configs requiring multi-signal validation
Trade-off: stricter ejection hysteresis increases time to react to genuine capacity loss but prevents oscillatory behavior; agreed default balances will be tuned with chaos experiments
Monitoring gap: we had regional fairness metrics but lacked a correlated KV-cache miss rate alert tied to variant shifts—added as priority
Review feedback: SRE suggested adding stochastic load tests that simulate locality skew to validate canary pipelines
Approval: PM and Head of Platform approved the proposed permanent fixes on 2026-03-13
validation_criteria: No more than 1% of routes experience >2x baseline p99 latency for 48h
Regional weight oscillation rate reduced to <1 event per 24h per region across next 7 days
Variant-shift spikes (percent of traffic moved to fallback variants) capped below 15% per route within any 10-minute window
